detailed_findings.finding: The reduction from 'all three points have color different from f(O)' to 'the triple is monochromatic' is valid because the codomain is exactly {red, green}.
The proof that A, B, C are noncollinear is complete: it justifies that any line intersects Circle(O,r) in at most two points via the quadratic equation DX^2 = r^2 - OD^2.
The identification circumcenter(A,B,C)=O is correctly obtained from OA=OB=OC together with noncollinearity, so the hypothesis P(f) applies directly.

reason: The proof is mathematically correct and complete. From the two-color assumption it correctly deduces that any three points on the circle with color different from f(O) are monochromatic. It then proves such a triple cannot be collinear because any line meets a circle in at most two points, identifies O as the circumcenter of the noncollinear triple using equal radii and perpendicular bisectors, and applies the hypothesis to obtain the contradiction f(O)=f(A). This matches the lemma statement exactly and aligns with the root theorem's use of the circumcenter property.
